mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding future equity value.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: In sample periods where FEDFUNDS > 4% for > 3 months, 20-day forward returns are non-negative with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) coinciding with falling unemployment (UNRATE) creates a labor market tightening that precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In 100 consecutive 5-day windows where UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases, forward returns are negative with p-value < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% month-over-month predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient demand for capital goods.
failure_condition: Over 5 consecutive quarters where INDPRO growth > 2%, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.5% for three consecutive months suggests a supply-side release, leading to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: During periods of sustained CPIAUCSL < 2.5%, 20-day forward returns remain positive with p-value < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.5 percentage points, the S&P 500 shows a negative 20-day forward return due to expectations of higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: In 10 pre-tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising MA > 0.5%), no 20-day forward return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) above 200,000 in a month coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals labor market fluidity and investor optimism.
failure_condition: In 50 loosening months where PAYEMS > 200k, 5-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not in observable list - so skip and use GDPC1 instead) - Correction: Use GDPC1 for demand. So: A 2% month-over-month increase in GDPC1 for two consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via momentum in business demand.
failure_condition: Over 10 recovery phases (GDPC1 up 2% m/m for 2 months), 20-day forward returns show no positive excess returns (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 4-week moving average of industrial production (INDPRO) falls by 3% or more, the S&P 500 exhibits a negative 60-day forward return as weak demand signals supply-side constraints.
failure_condition: During 5 supply shock episodes (INDPRO MA fall > 3%), 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).
